speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent, and I will be examining you today. Can you tell me your age and describe any symptoms you are currently experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is very reassuring to hear he is meeting milestones and has no known concerns. However, the instruction specifically asks me to evaluate him for systemic hypertension, so I need to check his blood pressure now. May I take his blood pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual finding, as hypertension is typically systemic rather than isolated to one arm. I need to check his blood pressure in both arms and both legs to see if there is a discrepancy in readings. REQUEST TEST: Blood Pressure All Four Extremities

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Pressure Right Upper Extremity: 150/80 mm Hg; Upper Extremities: 150/80 mm Hg (Right), Compared to lower values in lower extremities

speaker: Doctor
text: The significant discrepancy between upper and lower extremity blood pressures strongly suggests coarctation of the aorta. I need to visualize the aortic arch to confirm this structural defect. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: The echocardiogram confirms coarctation of the aorta with a pressure gradient. DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the aorta
